column5: **Databases:** keeping SQL in `.sql` files and generating constants works with any database: SQL Server and Azure SQL, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, Oracle, CockroachDB and others.  Describing queries

works with PostgreSQL 14 or later, and with SQL Server 2017 or later and Azure SQL, which is accepted and not tested; other databases are not described: see database support.  So with PostgreSQL or SQL Server, follow the five steps below: by default every query must be described, which step 5 does, and the build reports an error for each query until it is.  With any other database, follow steps 1 to 3 and set the output to `sql`, which gives you a constant for each query and needs no description, as Just want to keep your SQL out of code files? shows.  To run the queries yourself, through Dapper or your own ADO.NET code, see only generating models.
